review: Written by Claude from the lesson text. Check the English and the answers before using it with learners.

items.q: Prairie dogs dig with their strong teeth.
Prairie Dog Town has escape tunnels.
The guard stood on its hind legs to watch for danger.
Prairie dogs use colors to warn each other.
A family group of prairie dogs is called a coterie.
Prairie dogs eat insects, roots, and seeds.
Where did the prairie dogs peek out from?
items.why: “Little brown animals peeked out from holes in the ground.”

items.q: What were some prairie dogs pushing out of their burrows?
items.why: “Some were pushing dirt out of their burrows.”

items.q: Which animals might be dangerous for prairie dogs?
items.why: “Maybe a hawk was flying above. Maybe a coyote was nearby.”

items.q: What did some prairie dogs do when they heard the call?

blocks.title: 4. Open questions
blocks.note: These questions are open. Talk about your answers with your teacher or a classmate.

items.q: Without looking at the text, sum it up in three sentences.
items.model: Prairie dogs live under the prairie in a town of tunnels and chambers. A guard watches for danger and calls to warn the others. They live in family groups, and their burrows help other animals too.

items.q: What would we see if we could look under Prairie Dog Town?
items.model: We would see tunnels going in many directions, chambers for sleeping, safe places for babies and escape tunnels.
It stands on its hind legs and watches for danger. Then it gives a sharp call to warn the others.

items.q: How does Prairie Dog Town help other animals?
items.model: Sometimes other animals use old burrows for shelter.

items.q: Who keeps you safe at home and at school? How?

blocks.title: 5. Put in order
blocks.intro: Put the events in the order of the story.
items: Little brown animals peeked out from holes
Some prairie dogs were digging with their claws
One prairie dog stood very still and looked around
The guard gave a sharp call
Some prairie dogs ran to their burrows
